sections.hook: A translation moves every point of a shape the same distance in the same direction.
sections.core_explanation: A translation is described by a vector $\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}$. Each point (a,b) maps to (a+x, b+y). The shape is congruent to the original.
sections.worked_example:
**Question:** Translate triangle A(1,1), B(3,1), C(2,4) by vector $\begin{pmatrix}4\\-1\end{pmatrix}$.

**Solution:** A'(5,0), B'(7,0), C'(6,3)

common_mistakes.mistake: Adding vectors incorrectly by adding only x or only y components
common_mistakes.correction: Always add x-components together AND y-components together separately

common_mistakes.mistake: Confusing direction in rotations (clockwise vs anticlockwise)
common_mistakes.correction: Draw a simple diagram to verify the direction before calculating coordinates
